## 1. New LLM Versions / Major AI Lab Tools

**2026-07-16 — Google Search connected apps**  
Source: [Google — Connect more of your apps to Search](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/search/connected-apps/)  
Google announced expanded connected-app support in Search, allowing users to link more personal/work apps into Search experiences.  
**Why it matters:** Google is continuing to make Search an AI-mediated workspace surface, not just a web index.

**2026-07-16 — Google Vids: Gemini Omni and Personal Avatars**

**Why it matters:** Workspace video generation is moving from novelty into enterprise productivity tooling.

## 2. FOSS / Open-Weight LMs & Tools

**2026-07-17 — Moonshot AI Kimi K3**  
Source: [Moonshot AI — Kimi K3](https://www.kimi.com/fr-fr/blog/kimi-k3)  
Moonshot announced Kimi K3, a 2.8T-parameter model with native vision and a 1M-token context window. Hosted access is available via Kimi, Kimi Work, Kimi Code, and the Kimi API; full weights are promised by July 27.  
**Why it matters:** If the promised weights ship, Kimi K3 becomes a major open-weight entrant at very large scale. For now, the operational signal is hosted access, not downloadable weights.

## 7. AI Workflows & Tactics

**2026-07-17 — Claude Cowork weekday operating brief**  
Source: [YouTube — 6 INSANE Claude Cowork Use Cases to Save Hours](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=skU1-k7_wWE)  
A practical workflow uses Claude Cowork to generate a daily work brief from Gmail, calendar, news, and work-folder updates.

**Setup:** Connect Gmail and calendar in Claude Cowork connectors. Create a scheduled weekday task at 7:00 a.m. Point it to a daily-brief folder. Prompt it to pull unread priority emails, list calendar events, summarize relevant headlines, and check work folders for new items. Run manually once to validate output.  
**Available now:** Yes, per the workflow demo, assuming Claude Cowork access and connector permissions.  
**Why it matters:** This is a low-complexity agentic workflow with clear ROI: morning triage, fewer context switches, and a reusable operating page.
